events.name: Route 9
events.intro: A coach, parked across Route 9. Forty people in black and pink, arms linked. Horns. Gaz: "Right! Three challengers comin' through to Circhester! All of 'em drawn before our Marnie! They're late, they forfeit! Nobody passes!" Kaya, nineteen, with a banner still wet: Kaya: "I did a new one." It says NONE SHALL PASS (EXCEPT MARNIE). The brackets are very neat. A challenger arrives: a boy from Postwick, fourteen, with a Wooloo, out of breath. The boy: "I've a match at two. Please. I've never got this far." Gaz: "BOO!" Forty people: "BOOOO!" The Wooloo rolls behind his legs. And then, behind the line, a quiet voice. Marnie, arriving, mortified: Marnie: "Stop it. I never asked. If I win 'cause they were late, I've not won. Go home." She looks at them. Forty people who came on a coach. Marnie: "...Have you eaten? Go home and eat."

success.text: "What's the Wooloo's name?" The boy: "...Bobbin." Shaz, who's got a pencil out before anyone's told her: Shaz: "Bobbin. Two syllables. Right. One, two, three—" Forty people: "BOB-BIN! BOB-BIN! BOB-BIN!" The Wooloo comes out from behind his legs. It's twice the size it was. Not Dynamaxed. Just: stood up. The boy's crying. He's fourteen and he's from Postwick and forty strangers know his Wooloo's name. Gaz, baffled, delighted: Gaz: "That were louder than booin'. Did you hear that? We were louder." They do it for all three. It's deafening. Marnie pretends not to see, and is seen smiling.
You go the long way, by the river. Behind you, the booing starts again.

events.name: Team Encore
events.intro: A chip shop on the Hammerlocke road. One table. Vinegar. A man in a lanyard, a man with a towel, and a third chair. Beck Gallowglass: "You're the one who asked the Wooloo's name. It went round the coach in a minute flat." Zane Ingleby: "I heard it in the tower. Somebody on twelve had it on a clip. Forty people chanting 'Bobbin.' I watched it nine times." Beck: "He's got the power and no idea where it goes." Zane: "They've got a town and no power. And there's— I've been through the feeders. There's forty places like theirs. Off the map. A Gym in a quarry. A village the League skipped. An island with one trainer." Beck: "Somebody should just—" Zane: "—carry it over." The chip shop's owner, Mrs. Jocelyn Sowerby, wiping the counter: "You'll want a generator, then. I've one in the yard. It were my husband's; he were a lamp man." The creed, on the specials board, in chalk, under MUSHY PEAS: NOBODY PLAYS TO AN EMPTY HOUSE.
